props.gloss_en: the baraita as cited: what is the te'omet? from the te'omet inward, and the te'omet itself is as inward. RYbK: one slaughters only for the outer ones. RChbA: one pays no attention to the te'omet at all
what are the inner [gums]? from the te'omet inward, and the te'omet itself is as inward
where were these things said [that one does not slaughter]? where [the inner ones] were damaged or scratched
but [where the inner ones] were uprooted, one slaughters
RYbK: one slaughters only for the outer ones; for inner ones that were uprooted we do not slaughter
RYbK: but it is disqualified [from the altar]
RChbA: one pays no attention to the te'omet at all
RChbA: and it is not even disqualified
an internal lack of a limb counts as a lack
if [the dilemma is] for the firstborn: 'lame or blind' (Deut 15:21) is written
if for consecrated animals: 'blind or broken' (Lev 22:22) is written
for slaughtering and redeeming we have no dilemma; our dilemma is for disqualifying
horn 1: 'it shall be complete to be accepted' (Lev 22:21) -- complete, yes; lacking, no
horn 2: or perhaps 'complete... no blemish shall be in it': as a blemish is on the outside, so a lack is on the outside
'and the two kidneys' (Lev 3:4) -- and not one with one kidney
and not one with three kidneys
the other baraita: 'he shall remove it' -- to include one with one kidney
there is no creature [born] with one [kidney]; this one became lacking
(proposed) let us say they dispute this: one master holds an internal lack is a lack, the other that it is not
Rav Chiyya bar Yosef: all agree there is a creature [born] with one [kidney]
Rav Chiyya bar Yosef: here [the disqualifying baraita] -- where it was created with two and they became lacking
Rav Chiyya bar Yosef: there [the including baraita] -- where it was created with one from the outset
rather, here they dispute whether there is a creature [with one kidney] from the outset: one master holds there is, the other that there is not
R' Yochanan: here [the disqualifying baraita] -- where it became lacking before slaughter
R' Yochanan: there [the including baraita] -- where it became lacking after slaughter
Rav: one who slits the ear of the bull and afterwards receives its blood -- [the offering is] invalid
Rav: as it says 'and he shall take of the blood of the bull' (Lev 4:5) -- the bull that already was
rather: here -- where it became lacking before receiving [the blood]
there -- where it became lacking after receiving [the blood]
'a complete lamb, a male in its year, shall it be for you' (Ex 12:5) -- complete and in its year at the time of slaughter
and from where in receiving, conveying and sprinkling? 'shall it be' -- that all its stages be complete and in its year
interpret it [the baraita's 'all its stages'] as about being in its year [only]
R' Yehoshua: all offerings in the Torah of which an olive's bulk of flesh or an olive's bulk of fat remains -- he sprinkles the blood
Rava: that is to say, hours disqualify in consecrated offerings
the baraita as cited: 'bruised, crushed, torn, cut' (Lev 22:24) -- all of them in the testicles, the words of R' Yehuda
read: also in the testicles -- the words of R' Yehuda
REbY: all of them in the gid
R' Yosei: bruised and crushed -- also in the testicles
R' Yosei: torn and cut -- in the gid yes, in the testicles no
(proposed) do they not dispute this: one master holds an internal lack is a lack, the other that it is not?
on that hinge R' Yosei's split ruling fits neither side: if an internal lack is a lack, torn and cut too [would be blemishes]; if not, not even bruised and crushed
rather, here they dispute over visible blemishes
bruised and crushed [testicles] are a blemish
torn and cut [testicles] are a blemish
bruised and crushed [testicles] are not a blemish
torn and cut [testicles] are not a blemish
R' Yehuda's reason for bruised and crushed: they shrink
R' Yehuda's reason for torn and cut: they hang
REbY's reason for bruised and crushed: from the outset too they sometimes shrink
REbY's reason for torn and cut: from the outset too they sometimes hang
R' Yosei's reason for bruised and crushed being a blemish: they are not there
R' Yosei's reason for torn and cut not being a blemish: they are there

questions.gloss_en: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami asks: does an internal lack of a limb disqualify an offering? Neither תא שמע (the kidney baraitot, the maukh baraita) resolves it -- each is reread as another dispute -- and the text records no resolution and no תיקו

supports.gloss_en: תא שמע: ואת שתי הכליות -- not one kidney, not three; ותניא אידך: יסירנה -- to include one kidney. If no creature is born with one, the baraitot dispute whether an internal lack is a lack

deflected_by.gloss_en: דכולי עלמא יש בריה באחת וחסרון מבפנים שמיה חסרון, ולא קשיא: כאן כשנבראה בשתים וחסרו, כאן כשנבראה באחת מעיקרא

refuted_by.gloss_en: והא דומיא דשלש קתני -- one kidney is listed with three, so it too is from the outset (= obj_dumya_dishalosh)

deflected_by.gloss_en: אלא, הכא ביש בריה מעיקרא קמיפלגי (= p_kelayot_hinge_beriya)
דכולי עלמא אין בריה באחת וחסרון מבפנים שמיה חסרון, ולא קשיא: כאן שחסרה קודם שחיטה, כאן שחסרה לאחר שחיטה

refuted_by.gloss_en: והאמר רבי זירא אמר רב: הצורם אוזן הפר ואחר כך קיבל דמו פסול (= obj_tzorem_ozen)

deflected_by.gloss_en: אלא: כאן שחסרה קודם קבלה, כאן שחסרה לאחר קבלה (= p_okimta_kodem_kabbala, p_okimta_achar_kabbala; its attack at 39b.2 is answered at 39b.4)

supports.gloss_en: הכי נמי מסתברא, דתניא: רבי יהושע אומר ... זורק את הדם, שמע מינה -- even when most of the offering is gone after receiving, the blood is sprinkled, so completeness is not required at sprinkling
זאת אומרת -- the baraita, read as requiring the animal to be in its year at every stage, implies the year can end between them: hours disqualify

objections.gloss_en: מאי קאמר? ותו, רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי היינו תנא קמא! -- the baraita asks what the te'omet is and answers about the inner region; and RYbK says what the first tanna says

answered_by.gloss_en: חסורי מיחסרא והכי קתני -- the baraita is defective; it teaches the inner gums' extent, that damaged or scratched ones are not slaughtered but uprooted ones are, and RYbK and RChbA each go further (= the reconstructed props at 39a.13-14)

objections.gloss_en: והא דומיא דשלש קתני, מה שלש מעיקרא, אף אחת מעיקרא -- the baraita lists one kidney alongside three, and three are from the outset, so one is from the outset too. Unanswered: the stam turns to אלא (39a.22)
ולאחר שחיטה קודם קבלה מי שרי? והאמר רבי זירא אמר רב: הצורם אוזן הפר ואחר כך קיבל דמו פסול -- a blemish after slaughter but before receiving still disqualifies. Unanswered: the stam turns to אלא
ולאחר קבלה קודם זריקה מי שרי? והתניא: שה תמים ... יהיה -- all its stages, receiving, conveying and sprinkling, must be complete and in its year

answered_by.gloss_en: תרגמה אבן שנה -- the 'all its stages' clause is about being in its year only, not about being complete (= p_targema_aben_shana)

objections.gloss_en: ומי איכא מידי דבשעת שחיטה הוי בן שנה ובשעת קבלה והולכה הוי בן שתי שנים? -- can an animal be in its year at slaughter and in its second year at receiving?

answered_by.gloss_en: זאת אומרת שעות פוסלות בקדשים -- yes: age is reckoned by the hour, so the year can end between slaughter and receiving (= p_rava_shaot_poslot)

objections.gloss_en: בביצים ולא בגיד? -- in the testicles and not in the gid?

answered_by.gloss_en: אימא: אף בביצים -- read 'also in the testicles' (= p_ry_af_babeitzim)
